The variable `lastColon` is assigned the result of `ipString.lastIndexOf(':')`, which returns the index of the last colon or -1 if not found. The first call uses two arguments: beginIndex=0, endIndex=lastColon+1. For this to throw IndexOutOfBoundsException, one of the conditions must be: beginIndex < 0 (0 is not negative), endIndex > length of string, or beginIndex > endIndex. Since lastColon+1 is between 0 and length (because lastIndexOf returns -1 or an index in [0, length-1]), endIndex <= length always. Also, 0 <= lastColon+1 because lastColon+1 >= 0, so beginIndex <= endIndex. Thus, no exception. The second call uses one argument: beginIndex=lastColon+1. It throws if beginIndex < 0 or beginIndex > length. As argued, lastColon+1 >= 0 and <= length. Hence, both calls are safe under the given logic, assuming ipString is not null. The API documentation only declares IndexOutOfBoundsException, whose throwing conditions are fully avoided.
